question.text: Under the Foreign Exchange Management (Debt Instruments) Regulations, 2019, which of the following options lists instruments that FPIs can purchase on repatriation basis?

answer.text: Only equity shares and convertible debentures
Only dated Government securities and treasury bills
Only corporate bonds and debentures of Indian companies
Dated Government securities, non-convertible debentures/bonds, commercial papers, security receipts issued by ARCs, and municipal bonds

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the DI Regulations, FPIs may purchase on repatriation basis a list of debt instruments that includes dated Government securities and treasury bills, non-convertible debentures/bonds, commercial papers, units of eligible domestic mutual funds/ETFs, security receipts issued by ARCs, debt instruments issued by banks that are eligible for inclusion as regulatory capital, credit-enhanced bonds, listed NCDs/redeemable preference shares, securitised debt instruments, rupee-denominated bonds/units issued by IDFs, municipal bonds, and exchange-traded derivative contracts approved by SEBI. Option D contains a valid subset of these permissible instruments. The Trap: Equity shares and convertible debentures fall under the non-debt instrument framework (FDI/FPI equity), not under the Debt Instruments Regulations, so option A is incorrect. Note: Pages 221-222 list the permissible FPI debt instruments and page 223 provides the non-debt context; the list in option D is illustrative rather than exhaustive.
